verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:34 — "4. But grep -inE "install|dependenc|baseline|checkpoint|context-restore|clean state|clean tree" over SKILL.md (the skill's only file — the directory contains SKILL.md and nothing else) returns nothing about installing deps, confirming a clean baseline, or context-restore; the four hits (31, 39, 106, 197) are about plan dependencies, orchestrator models, workflow checkpoints and gate checkpoints. verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:132 — "- **TDD-first is the default task contract.** Every implementation task: write the failing test, watch it fail, implement, watch it pass, commit. Subagents follow the test-driven-development skill; the dispatch prompt says so explicitly."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 569-570. The skill sentence at line 132 is verbatim as quoted and covers all three elements of the KICKOFF clause: it names test-driven-development, spells out the red-green loop ("write the failing test, watch it fail, implement, watch it pass"), and commits to injecting it. Stronger than the claim knew: the skill's own dispatch machinery hard-codes it — references/workflows/sprint-execution.workflow.mjs line 254 pushes "- TDD-first. For every implementation task: write the failing test, watch it fail, implement, watch it pass, commit. Follow the test-driven-development skill." into every track prompt. TDD is not a mode the skill leaves open, so this is not mode selection; it is re-teaching the skill's own default contract.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:156 — "Tests: <suite result one-liner>" (the close-handover field, with no evidence requirement attached), against SKILL.md:180 — "A handover's `Merged` field is a self-report, not evidence; this check is the evidence", which applies that standard to merges ONLY.

The skill directory holds only SKILL.md (ls confirms, no references/ subdir), so I also grepped the plugin-root references the skill cites — independent-review.md, complexity-signals.md, doc-sitemap.md, workflows/sprint-execution.workflow.mjs. Broad grep -inE "verification-before|fresh|command output|evidence|confidence|proof|self-report|actually ran|re-run|verif" over SKILL.md returns 20 hits, none of which impose an evidence standard on a done-claim: 180 is merge-specific, 185 makes verification subagents "Optional", 217 defers to "verifications the plan specifies", 195 is about reviewer 'cannot verify from diff' items. The nearest real coverage the claim missed is line 193 ("each fix dispatch names the covering test files and carries the contract to re-run them and report results") and line 132's watch-it-pass loop — genuine but scoped to fix dispatches and to the subagent's own inner loop, not to the orchestrator accepting a track's completion claim. The workflow schema (workflow.mjs:159) defines tests as "One-line suite result" with no proof obligation, and the built dispatch contract (lines 252-273) never asks for command output. Gap confirmed: the KICKOFF text is load-bearing and must be KEPT; the fix belongs in the skill (an evidence rule on the Tests/Status fields mirroring §6.2's treatment of `Merged`).

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:8 — "Execute a written plan by dispatching subagents — one per track — in parallel waves, each in an isolated git worktree, with the orchestrator owning merges, state, and gates."

I checked all four clauses against the skill individually: per-track worktree dispatch = line 8 and §3 lines 46-54; two-stage review gates = line 192 "**Per-track/per-wave review:**" and line 194 "**Final whole-branch review:** after all waves, run one broad review over `merge-base..HEAD`"; compaction-proof ledger = line 21 "| Progress ledger | `docs/state/sprint/progress.md` | Compaction-proof recovery map" and §6.6 line 184; central merge = line 53 "**The orchestrator merges** every returned branch" and §6.1 line 179. Every clause is architecture the skill fixes for itself; nothing here is an argument the operator supplies, no path, mode, condition or ordering. Straight restatement of the skill's own methodology.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:180 — "2. **Verify the merge mechanically:** `git log <integration-branch>..<branch> --oneline` must come back **empty** for every branch. A handover's `Merged` field is a self-report, not evidence; this check is the evidence."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 574-576. The skill sentence at line 180 is verbatim as quoted, down to the identical git command, the identical "must come back empty for every branch", and the identical "a handover's `Merged` field is a self-report, not evidence" phrasing. The skill enforces it twice more: line 212 "Accept a track's `Merged` field as proof it merged — verify with `git log <integration-branch>..<branch>` (§6.2)" and line 214 "Start Wave N+1 with unmerged Wave-N branches, or before §6.2 verification passes". Nothing in the KICKOFF sentence parameterises the gate — no branch names are supplied, both are left as the same placeholders the skill uses. Near-verbatim re-derivation of a hard rule; high severity is right.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:55-56 — "- **One wave per Workflow run.** Wave N+1 is dispatched only after the integration branch contains all of Wave N's merged work, so the next wave's worktrees inherit it."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 576-577. Both clauses are covered, and the 'so invoke it again for each wave' consequence is spelled out by the skill itself: line 102 "**ONE wave per run — there is no `waves[]` array, and passing one throws.** … Wave N+1 is a separate invocation, made only after §6 has merged and verified Wave N."; line 134 "The orchestrator **must not start Wave N+1** until all Wave N subagents have returned and their worktrees are merged (§6)"; line 186 "8. Only then start Wave N+1, as a **new Workflow run**."; red flags at 206 and 214. Five separate statements in the skill, mechanically enforced (passing a waves[] array throws). The KICKOFF supplies no parameter or condition the skill lacks.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:194 — "- **Final whole-branch review:** after all waves, run one broad review over `merge-base..HEAD` on the most capable model."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 577-579. The skill knows its own two review stages (lines 192 and 194) and even contemplates project-defined adversarial rounds (line 196: "adversarial review rounds after merges via `code-review-gate` in round mode"), but it cannot know that the surrounding pipeline runs a separate adversarial phase-level review at step 10 against the whole built phase. Pure cross-step disambiguation, and it is doing real work: line 196 explicitly invites project-defined gates to be folded in, which is exactly the confusion this parenthetical forecloses. Not a contradiction with anything in the skill. KEEP.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:198 — "- **After the final whole-branch review comes back clean**, the sprint's implementation work is done — invoke the finishing-a-development-branch skill to verify tests one last time and present the merge/PR/keep/discard decision."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 583-585. The skill sentence at line 198 is verbatim as quoted and matches clause for clause: the same trigger condition ('after the final whole-branch review comes back clean'), the same handoff target, and the same four-option menu. Also restated as red flag line 219. The duplication is real, so the claim survives. I downgraded severity from medium to low: the excluded tail of the KICKOFF sentence ("so the last wave of this phase will surface that menu right here, at step 8") is pipeline-positioning the skill cannot know, and this restatement is the grammatical antecedent for the load-bearing 'Take keep' directive (claim 9) — trimming it wins one clause at a real cohesion cost.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:198 (same bullet, final sentence) — "Don't decide that disposition yourself; it's the skill's call to make with the user."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF quote verified at lines 585-589. The skill explicitly refuses to pick a disposition and hands the choice to the user (line 198, reinforced by red flag line 219 "Merge, PR, or discard the sprint branch yourself after the final review — hand off to finishing-a-development-branch instead"). The KICKOFF is the user's standing answer plus the pipeline-level justification — four downstream gates at steps 10, 11, 12 and 13 — which no skill can know. I checked the contradiction reading and rejected it: the menu is still surfaced, and the final sentence ("If I answer anything other than keep, say plainly which gates I am skipping") presupposes the user may answer differently, so the skill's user-decides rule is preserved rather than overridden. Fills exactly the hole the skill leaves open. KEEP.
